name: Web Crypto (non-extractable keys)
plain: Provides built-in cryptography; keys can be stored in the browser and marked non-exportable.
meaning: A site can encrypt data, sign with keys it cannot export, and store them in IndexedDB. Non-extractable keys stop theft by script but do not stop a malicious page using them.

access.persistence: CryptoKey objects can be stored in IndexedDB as opaque handles
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: HTTPS only (crypto.subtle undefined on HTTP except localhost)

limits.headline: Can lock and unlock data inside the page, with keys it can't hand out
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page signs in, saves data or checks a file.
can: Create secure keys and random numbers
Check that a file has not been changed
cannot: Hand out a key that was made non exportable
Reach keys saved by other sites
Work on a page that is not on a secure connection (HTTPS)
Keep its saved keys after you clear that site's data

story.what_it_is: The browser has built in locks and keys that a page can use and store safely.

marketing.name: Web Crypto API
marketing.pitch: MDN says the API gives pages tools for hashing, signing, encryption and key handling.

story.for_you: You never see it. It quietly protects logins, chats and payments, and keeps your keys in a form that scripts cannot read out.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to secure logins, sign messages and encrypt data in your browser before it leaves. Non exportable keys help stop theft even if the page is attacked.

use_cases.example: A secure chat tool encrypts messages in your browser before sending.
A bank page signs a login challenge with a key that never leaves the browser.
A password manager web app encrypts your vault locally.
A notes app does end to end encryption of your documents.
A browser game signs scores so cheaters cannot send fake ones.
Ad scripts use random numbers from the same tool to create ids.

technical_bounds: Non-extractable keys cannot be exported via exportKey(), but any script on the origin can use them
getRandomValues fills at most 65536 bytes per call
Algorithms: AES-GCM and CBC and CTR, RSA-OAEP and PSS, ECDSA (P-256, P-384, P-521), ECDH, HMAC, HKDF, PBKDF2, SHA-1/256/384/512; Ed25519 (Chrome 137, Safari 17, Firefox 129), X25519
No hardware-backed keys (use WebAuthn for that)
